newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds slightly off in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds slightly off in thin trade.

text.p: Irish bonds eased slightly in thin trade on Wednesday, underperforming against other peripheral markets such as Spain and Italy, dealers said.

"It's been a very quiet day and Irish bonds have failed to keep up with Spain and Italy," a dealer said. "Having said that, the 10-year bonds have held in quite well -- just off yesterday's auction level."
With just 120 million Irish pounds bid for the 80 million Irish pounds of 2006 stock auctioned yesterday, dealers described the response as disappointing.
By 1510 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down two pence at 102.07 to yield 5.94 percent, while the eight percent bond due 2006 was down seven pence at 109.85 to yield 6.53 percent.
Yields against German Bunds were off by about three basis points at 156 basis points over in the five-year bond, and unchanged from the close at 81 over in the 10-year.
Dealers said the broad-based EMU suggested by the outcome of yesterday's EU summit in Amsterdam would favour Spain and Italy, "given French and German difficulties".
The stability pact, agreed at the summit, was seen as generally favourable for peripheral bond markets.
Yesterday's deal tying employment and growth to fiscal discipline had cleared the way for a timely start of Europe's single currency in 1999, analysts agreed.
Looking ahead, dealers said, the Irish backdrop was supportive of bonds.
"A redemption of one billion Irish pounds of the 1997 bond in July will mean a lot of cash for re-investment and the supply and demand mismatch will support bond prices, one dealer said.
In the UK on Wednesday, gilts lost further to Bunds after stronger-than-expected UK retail data raised fears of an interest rate hike and set a negative tone.
